title: Verse Summary of the Avataṃsaka Sutra

source.text: Verse Summary of the Avataṃsaka Sutra by Nāgārjuna: a chanting text summarizing in 7-character verses the assembly of the 80-fascicle Avataṃsaka, Sudhana's spiritual friends, and the names of its 39 chapters
source.license: Original text: traditional chanting text, public domain
source.translationLicense: English translation and commentary: newly made by Sutra Box from its own Korean version (based on an AI draft, still being reviewed and refined)

k01.heading: Title and Refuge
k01.plain: The Great Expansive Buddha Flower Garland Sutra, in verses summarized by Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva. I take refuge in Vairocana, the true Dharma body of the ocean of worlds adorned with lotuses; in Rocana Buddha, now teaching the Dharma; in Śākyamuni and all the Tathāgatas; and in all the great sages of past, present and future in the ten directions. By the power of the ocean-seal samādhi they turn the fundamental Dharma wheel of the Flower Garland,
k01.commentary: It begins by calling in turn on the three bodies of the Buddha: Vairocana (Dharma body), Rocana (reward body) and Śākyamuni (manifest body). As a chanting text for reciting the whole Avataṃsaka Sutra in brief, it is often chanted for the merit of recitation.

k02.heading: The Guardian Spirits of the Assembly
k02.plain: Samantabhadra and the great assembly gathered, with vajra-holding spirits and body-guarding spirits, footstep-guarding spirits and spirits of the practice place, spirits of cities, earth, mountains and forests, spirits of medicine, grain, rivers and seas, spirits of water, fire, wind and space, spirits of directions, night and day, and the asuras.
k02.commentary: This is the assembly gathered in the first chapter, The Wondrous Adornments of the Rulers of the World. Spirits who watch over everything in the world protect the gathering. The guardian-spirit altar in Korean temples comes from this assembly.

k03.heading: The Eight Kinds of Beings and the Heavens
k03.plain: Garuḍa kings and kiṃnaras, mahoragas and yakṣa kings, great dragon kings and kumbhāṇḍas, gandharva kings and the son of the moon, the son of the sun and the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma heaven king and the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati heaven king and the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, the Great Brahmā king and the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna heaven king and the Bṛhatphala Heaven, up to the Maheśvara heaven king: more than words can tell.
k03.commentary: The eight kinds of beings who protect the Dharma and the many heavens of the desire and form realms have all gathered.

k04.heading: Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas
k04.plain: The great bodhisattvas Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī; the bodhisattvas Dharma Wisdom, Forest of Merit, Vajra Banner, Vajra Treasury, Vajra Wisdom, Blazing Light Banner and Sumeru Banner; the śrāvakas of great virtue, Śāriputra and the monk Ocean Awakening; laymen and laywomen; Sudhana and the boys and girls: their number is measureless and cannot be told.
k04.commentary: The bodhisattvas Dharma Wisdom, Forest of Merit, Vajra Banner and Vajra Treasury are the ones who teach the ten abodes, ten practices, ten dedications and ten grounds of the Avataṃsaka Sutra.

k05.heading: Sudhana's Spiritual Friends (1)
k05.plain: Of the spiritual friends Sudhana met, Mañjuśrī was the first; then the monks Meghaśrī, Sāgaramegha and Supratiṣṭhita; Megha and the elder Muktaka and the monk Sāradhvaja; the laywoman Āśā and the sage Bhīṣmottaranirghoṣa; the brahmin Jayoṣmāyatana and the maiden Maitrāyaṇī; the monk Sudarśana and the boy Indriyeśvara; the laywoman Prabhūtā and the householder Vidvān; the elder Ratnacūḍa and the elder Samantanetra; King Anala and King Mahāprabha.
k05.commentary: In the Entering the Dharma Realm chapter, Sudhana visits fifty-three spiritual friends in turn. The point of the story is to learn from anyone: monastics, merchants, kings, women, children, even followers of other paths.

k06.heading: Sudhana's Spiritual Friends (2)
k06.plain: The laywoman Acalā and the wandering ascetic Sarvagāmin; the elder Utpalabhūti; the ferryman Vaira and the elder Jayottama; the nun Siṃhavijṛmbhitā and the woman Vasumitrā; the householder Veṣṭhila; Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Ananyagāmin Bodhisattva; the god Mahādeva and the earth goddess Sthāvarā; the night goddess Vāsantī, the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, and the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
k06.commentary: "The Freely Observing One" is Avalokiteśvara. Sudhana meets Avalokiteśvara on Mount Potalaka.

k07.heading: Sudhana's Spiritual Friends (3)
k07.plain: The night goddess who saves all beings with wondrous virtue; the night goddesses of the ocean of quiet sound, of protecting all, of blooming trees, and of great vows and vigorous rescue; the goddess Sutejomaṇḍalaratiśrī and the woman Gopā; Queen Māyā and the heavenly maiden Surendrābhā; the teacher Viśvāmitra and the boy Śilpābhijña; the laywoman Bhadrottamā and the elder Muktāsāra; the elder Sucandra and the elder Ajitasena; the brahmin Śivarāgra; the boy Śrīsaṃbhava and the girl Śrīmati; then Maitreya Bodhisattva and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and finally Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and an assembly as countless as dust.
k07.commentary: Sudhana's pilgrimage passes through Maitreya and Mañjuśrī and is completed with Samantabhadra. It means that awakening (Mañjuśrī) is brought to completion in practice (Samantabhadra).

k08.heading: The Dharma Ever Taught
k08.plain: Gathering like clouds at this assembly, they always follow Vairocana Buddha, and in the ocean of the Lotus Treasury World they grandly turn the great Dharma wheel. In all the worlds throughout the space of the ten directions, the Dharma is always taught in the same way.
k08.commentary: The Avataṃsaka assembly is not something of one time and place; it is always open in every world.

k09.heading: The Thirty-Nine Chapters (1)
k09.plain: Six, six, six, four, three, one, eleven, one, one: these are the chapters of the nine assemblies in seven places. The Wondrous Adornments of the Rulers of the World, The Appearance of the Tathāgata, Samantabhadra's Samādhi, The Formation of the Worlds, The Flower Treasury World, Vairocana, The Names of the Tathāgata, The Four Noble Truths, Awakening by Light, The Bodhisattvas' Questions, Pure Conduct, Chief in Goodness, Ascending the Peak of Sumeru, Verses of Praise on Sumeru's Peak, The Ten Abodes, Pure Practice, The Merit of First Arousing the Mind, Clarifying the Dharma.
k09.commentary: The first two lines simply list in numbers how many chapters were taught at each of the nine assemblies (6+6+6+4+3+1+11+1+1 = 39).

k10.heading: The Thirty-Nine Chapters (2)
k10.plain: Ascending to Yāma's Palace, Verses of Praise in Yāma's Palace, The Ten Practices, The Ten Inexhaustible Treasuries, Ascending to the Tuṣita Palace, Verses of Praise in the Tuṣita Palace, The Ten Dedications, The Ten Grounds, The Ten Concentrations, The Ten Powers, The Ten Acceptances, The Asaṃkhyeya, Lifespan, The Dwelling Places of Bodhisattvas, The Inconceivable Qualities of the Buddha, The Ocean of Marks of the Tathāgata's Ten Bodies, The Merit of the Tathāgata's Light, Samantabhadra's Practice, The Appearance of the Tathāgata, Detachment from the World, Entering the Dharma Realm.
k10.commentary: The stages of the bodhisattva path, from the ten abodes and ten practices to the ten dedications and ten grounds, show plainly in the chapter names. The last chapter, Entering the Dharma Realm, is the story of Sudhana's pilgrimage.

k11.heading: Conclusion
k11.plain: This is the sutra of a hundred thousand verses, the perfect teaching in thirty-nine chapters. Whoever recites it, believes it, receives and keeps it, at the moment they first arouse the mind attains right awakening; the one seated at ease in such an ocean of lands is called Vairocana Buddha.
k11.commentary: "The first arousal of the mind is right awakening" is a core line of the Avataṃsaka, found also in the Ode to the Dharma Nature.

vairocana.definition: The Buddha as truth itself (Dharma-body Buddha), shining light throughout the universe; the principal Buddha of the Avataṃsaka Sutra.

sudhana.definition: The seeker of the Entering the Dharma Realm chapter who, urged by Mañjuśrī, visits and learns from fifty-three spiritual friends and finally fulfills Samantabhadra's practice.
